1. Introduction :

The Government of Tamil Nadu launched a “Scheme for Free

Distribution of Goats / Sheep” for the poorest of poor in the rural

areas in order to enhance their standard of living during the year 2011-12.

The Scheme has been well appreciated for its success in converting an

assetless individuals into animal asset owning families having a

sustainable livelihood opportunity. The Scheme is being continued for the

year 2016-17.

1.1 A total of 1,00,000 beneficiaries who are predominantly women in rural

areas will be distributed 4 Goats / Sheep each during 2016-17 so as to have

a sustainable livelihood opportunity. As per the provisional figures available

under the 19th Livestock Census, there are about 81.43 lakh Goats and

47.86 lakh Sheep in the State. The following varieties of goats are

widely available in the State Salem Black, Kanni Aadu, Kodi Aadu, Non-

descriptive goat, Pallaiadu and Molai Aadu. The following types of sheep

are available in the State Meichery, Madras Red, Trichy Black, Ramnad

White, Vembur, Nilgiris and Keezha Karisal. Sheep are generally preferred

to be reared by the beneficiaries only in large numbers and that too in

such Village Panchayats which have got a lot of grazing grounds. Since

sheep are not fed through stall feeding, Goats can be maintained through

stall feeding in the households and are maintained even in such villages

where the grazing grounds are not extensively available. Goats are generally

preferred by poor households since it is possible to rear Goats even in a few

numbers. Hence, the people owning Goats are larger in number, whereas,

the Sheep owners are lesser in number. The rearing of goats is, however,

prohibited in some of the Village Panchayats which are bordering the forest

area in order to protect young trees from the browsing of goats.

2. Implementation of the Scheme :

2.1 The Goats / Sheep can normally be procured from within the State.

The procurement of Goats / Sheep in larger numbers from the other

States is not preferable since this category of animals (also called ‘small

ruminants’ in Veterinary terminology) are fragile and prone to diseases

when transported en masse from long distances and different climatic

zones. Hence, unlike the Scheme for procurement of free Milch Cows

wherein cows only from other States are proposed to be procured, it has

been decided to procure Goats/Sheep predominantly from the local market

ABSTRACT

Information Technology Department-Formation of State Level Coordination Committee for Common Service Centres (CSCs) - Orders - Issued.

From the Director of e-Governance, letter No.P/1 1/186/2016-TNeGA, dated 20.09.2016

ORDER:

Government Services as well as other private services are provided to the common man through Common Service Centres (CSCs) run by Primary Agriculture Co-operative Credit Societies (PACCS), Village Poverty Reduction Committee under Pudhu Vazhvu Project (VPRC), Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable TV Corporation Ltd (TACTV) Centres and Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu (ELCOT) Centres. At present, 5 Revenue Schemes, 6 Social Welfare Schemes and 8 Scholarship schemes for Students (educational assistance) are available in e-District portal as a single window system managed through Common Service Centres (CSCs).

2. In the letter read above, the Director, e-Governance/ CEO,TNEGA has _ requested that implementation and functioning of CSCs need to be monitored closely and problems/difficulties faced by CSCs need to be addressed, as and when it arises and therefore has sent a proposal for constitution of a State Level Coordination Committee for Common Service Centres.

3. After careful examination, the Government have decided to accept the above proposal and here by constitute a State Level Coordination Committee for Common Service Centres (CSCs) with the following composition:-

Director of e-Governance /Chief Executive Chairman Officer, Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency (TNeGA) Joint Director (Administration), Directorate of | Member e-Governance, Chennai Convener Additional Registrar (Finance and Banking), Member Primary Agriculture Co-operative Credit Societies (PACCS)

Additional Project Director, Pudhu Vazhvu Member Project (VPRC). Additional Director (P&C), Tamil Nadu State | Member Rural Livelihood Mission.

General Manager (e-Governance), Electronic Member Corporation of Tamil Nadu (ELCOT) General Manager (Operations), Tamil Nadu Member Arasu Cable TV Corporation Limited (TACTV)

The Committee will meet at least once in a month (or) as and when required to discuss the issues relating to the implementation/ functioning of Common Service Centres (CSCs). The Committee will also monitor the implementation and functioning of CSCs and send necessary recommendations / suggestions to the concerned Agencies/Departments to resolve the problems/difficulties faced by Common Service Centres (CSCs).

4. This order issues with the concurrence of Cooperation, Food and Consumer Protection Department and Rural Development and Panchyat Raj Departments

By order of the Governor)
